analysis:
Examined four changes.

(1) EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift head 38-41 adds the exact ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged list. The kill switch, crash-loop guard, VLM veto and explicit-selection semantics (head 49-107) are unchanged. An automatic paged construction failure still degrades (degradesPagedFailure). This only adds exact-ID matching; it adds no alias or substring match. No trust or attestation impact was identified. The larger default serving width is an availability/memory-admission concern for TB-007/T-029, which the docs say native memory admission still bounds.

(2) FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift head 70-92 adds maskCacheKey and allowsChainedDecode.
- Local reasoning is consistent. A .matched node returns key -1 and allowedTokenIDs returns answerStops (base 64). A .scanning node delegates to base.allowedTokenIDs(baseState) (base 65-66), so reusing the base key is sound.
- Non-negative base keys are enforced, so they cannot collide with -1. The method returns nil when resources are exhausted or the budget is spent, matching allowedTokenIDs returning [].

Open integration questions, in submodule source not supplied (libs/mlx-swift-lm bumped 889fe3c→0349802):
(a) Is the engine's device-mask cache scoped per constraint instance or request? Base state integers from different requests' constraints (different tool specs or stops) are not comparable. A cross-request cache keyed only by Int would apply another request's mask. The impact would be output integrity (T-007 class) and constraint bypass, not plaintext disclosure.
(b) Chained decode safety relies on nextState/intern (a mutating, lock-protected step) running only for host-confirmed tokens, as the comment claims. That redraw/restore logic, including the penalty and RNG restoration claimed in the docs at inference.md 2172-2184, lives in the submodule.

(3) The submodule bump is unreviewed and a coverage limit; it is not evidence of safety.

(4) The inference.md documentation additions (2172-2184) are consistent with the code.

No confidentiality, attestation (TB-009/TB-011), billing or prefix-cache (T-041) controls are touched.
